title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, is suing the city of Fargo, North Dakota, and police detective Lucas Heck for $10 million after being falsely arrested and jailed for about six months. She was taken at gunpoint from her home in July 2025 while babysitting four children, then held nearly four months without bail awaiting extradition and about two more months in North Dakota on theft and identity fraud charges. The charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee at the time of the Fargo fraud, and she was released on Christmas Eve.

The federal lawsuit says Fargo police relied on AI facial recognition that matched her social media photo to a fake ID used by a suspect in surveillance video, even though Lipps did not resemble the suspect and had never been to North Dakota. It alleges Heck requested an arrest warrant without enough probable cause and that the department lacked policies and training for facial recognition use. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and property and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation.
